problems.title: The strong-convexity bound omits infeasible initial error
claim: Theorem 6 gives objective-gap decay proportional to \(e^{-2\mu t}\) without requiring feasible initialization.
analysis: Let \(f(s,r)=((s-1)^2+r^2)/2\), \(h(s,r)=s\), \(T=I,K=1,\mu=1\), with initial point \((-1,0)\). The constraints have full row rank and the Hessian is \(I\). The exact flow is \(s=-e^{-t},r=0\). Its constrained-optimum objective gap is \(e^{-t}+e^{-2t}/2\), whereas the claimed envelope is \(3e^{-2t}/2\). At \(t=\log2\), these are \(5/8\) and \(3/8\). Convergence still occurs; the claimed envelope does not.
result: The quantitative strong-convexity envelope fails at an allowed infeasible initialization; convergence itself survives this example.
assumptions: The exact source version and operative conditions stated in this analysis.
repair: Require feasible initialization for the projected-gradient proof, or add an explicit normal-infeasibility term.
problems.impact_rationale: An exact strongly convex flow violates the theorem's objective envelope from an allowed infeasible initialization.
problems.existing_correction_status: Proposed correction; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.

problems.title: Finite squared-residual integral does not imply terminal convergence
problems.source_location: Theorems 1,4, pp.4–7; terminal-limit proofs, p.21 and Appendix E, p.25.
claim: Theorems \(1\) and \(4\) conclude that last-time KKT gaps vanish from a finite integral bound.
analysis: Let \(\phi\) be a smooth compactly supported unit-height bump and \(g(s)=1/(1+s^2)+\frac12\sum_{k\ge1}\phi((s+k)/2^{-k-3})\). Define \(F(s)=\int_{-\infty}^s g(u)\,du\), \(f(s,r)=F(s)\), \(h=r\), \(T=I,K=1\). The sum is locally finite; \(f\) is smooth, lower bounded and has bounded gradient.

The exact flow is \(\dot s=-g(s),\dot r=-r\). It crosses every \(s=-k\) at times tending to infinity, where the KKT residual is at least \(1/2\). Nonetheless \(\int g(s(t))^2dt=\int g(s)\,ds\) along the descending trajectory is finite. Narrowing peaks preserve finite integral without a vanishing terminal residual. The source's Jacobian/multiplier assumptions do not supply the missing uniform continuity.
result: A finite residual integral does not ensure the claimed last-time KKT convergence without an additional regularity condition.
assumptions: The exact source version and operative conditions stated in this analysis.
repair: Add and verify a condition implying uniform continuity of the residual, then use an appropriate integral-to-limit theorem. The integral and best-iterate guarantees are not refuted.
problems.impact_rationale: A smooth admissible flow has finite integrated squared residual but persistent terminal peaks, refuting the central integral-to-last-iterate conclusion.
problems.existing_correction_status: Proposed correction; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.

problems.title: The specified momentum merit can initially increase
claim: Theorem 5 gives numerical thresholds intended to make its particular merit function nonincreasing.
analysis: Use \(f(x)=0.01\log\cosh x\), \(h(x)=10^{-4}x\), \(T=K=1\), \(a_1=1,a_2=100000,\alpha=200000\), \(x_0=0.1,z_0=0\). Bounds \(M=1,D=20000,L_f=0.01,L_1=100,L_2=1.04\) satisfy the printed thresholds \(a_2\ge93200\) and \(\alpha\ge108003.05\). Direct differentiation of the full stated merit gives \(0.01[0.01\operatorname{sech}^2(0.1)-0.001]\simeq8.9006629\times10^{-5}>0\). This refutes its nonincrease claim, not stability under every alternative energy.
result: The theorem’s own sufficient constants permit a positive derivative of its stated merit function, disproving its nonincrease claim.
assumptions: The exact source version and operative conditions stated in this analysis.
repair: Rework the specific merit/threshold proof; no complete general replacement theorem is asserted.
problems.impact_rationale: The full printed merit increases despite satisfying the stated numerical thresholds. This directly refutes a central formal descent guarantee.
problems.existing_correction_status: Proposed correction; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.

problems.title: The OPF code omits the complementarity absolute value
problems.source_location: Paper KKT-gap definition, p.6; two OPF MATLAB metric paths.
claim: The paper defines KKT gap using the absolute value of lambda-transpose h.
analysis: The paper's gap uses \(|\lambda^\top h|\), while both author MATLAB metric paths insert the signed \(\lambda^\top h\) into a maximum with nonnegative residuals. A large negative value is then hidden. This is a local metric-definition mismatch; corrected OPF curves require the original per-step values.
result: The public OPF metric omits the absolute value in the declared complementarity term. Historical curves cannot be corrected without their per-step values.
assumptions: The exact source version and operative conditions stated in this analysis.
repair: Use \(|\lambda^\top h|\) consistently in that metric.
problems.impact_rationale: This establishes the stated local correction or limitation. A consequential failure of the paper's central result has not been demonstrated.
problems.existing_correction_status: Proposed correction; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.
